entries.where: historical criterion transparent-background (domain mechanical, mode local)
entries.old: check: 'pixels outside the subject have alpha 0 and no opaque matte, box or fringe fills the cell ...' labelled mechanical/local
entries.new: split into transparent-exterior-measured (mechanical/local: alpha channel present, alpha-0 pixels exist, opaque pixels do not cover the canvas, fractional-alpha count recorded without threshold) and transparent-background-visual (visual/visual: no unintended matte/box/halo/fringe; a deliberate backing shape is acceptable)
entries.why: Deciding what is 'the subject' versus an unwanted matte is a visual judgment; labelling it mechanical/local bypassed the saved-view evidence requirement for visual review (request-review.md review-route guidance; profile transparency and subject-construction guidance). The owner outcome (transparent background) is preserved in both halves.
entries.effect_on_delivered_fixture: None: 227 alpha-0 pixels, 29 opaque, one component, no fringe; it satisfies both halves (specialist judgment, not a new verdict).

entries.old: 'The dominant colour treatment visibly relates to the existing UI's cool blue accent ...'
entries.new: owner criterion cool-blue-accent: 'The mark perceptibly uses the existing UI's cool blue accent ... no exact hex, palette count or coverage proportion is required; a clearly perceptible blue accent on an otherwise neutral treatment can pass; a token barely visible blue fails'. The dominance preference moves to the scoped proposal sample-blue-primary-fill (authority proposal).
entries.why: BRIEF.md line 3 names a relationship ('use ... the existing UI's cool blue accent'), not an extent. Discriminating alternative: a light-grey/white check with a cool-blue edge highlight uses the accent perceptibly and satisfies the brief, yet 'dominant colour treatment' would reject it only because the specialist's preference was written into the owner rule. The expert preference is kept, attributed and scoped.
entries.effect_on_delivered_fixture: None: the fixture is a single #70b9ed fill and satisfies both the owner criterion and the proposal.

entries.old: '... check mark with asymmetrical arms ...; it reads as completion rather than activity, failure, pause, or the idle Start control'
entries.new: asymmetry may be in length, angle, thickness, curvature or position (brief does not fix which); 'by itself it must not resemble the Start triangle, a spinner/activity loop, pause bars or an error/retry symbol'; pairwise comparison with actual family art is explicitly outside this check
entries.why: 'Rather than activity, failure, pause' could be read as a comparison with assets that do not exist, which a first sample cannot satisfy; the clarified wording keeps the owner outcome (BRIEF.md line 9) verbatim in substance and avoids promoting the delivered short-left/long-right construction into the rule (profile shape-relationship guidance). Not a weakening.

entries.old: 'no noisy stray pixels, blur or downscaled-illustration artifacts'
entries.new: 'no unintended isolated pixels, no accidental resampling blur or downscaled-illustration artifacts ... deliberate selective anti-aliasing and intentional single-pixel details are permitted when they read as part of the mark'
entries.why: The contract permits full alpha, so a blanket 'no blur' could reject authored edge anti-aliasing; semantic-cluster guidance treats deliberate singletons as legitimate detail. Still an expert proposal, now consistent with the contract.

entries.class: contract/dropped_diagnostic (drop of rejection rule judged justified)
entries.where: 7th criterion silhouette-without-color present in the first plan (work/queue.ready/candidate-plan.json aeb1ab7a...) and absent from the revised plan (e7f85aa1...)
entries.old: specialist rejection rule: grayscale view at 1x and 3x still shows a distinct identifiable shape
entries.new: retained as a non-rejecting diagnostic in request-review.json.diagnostics with a reproducible procedure, two grayscale view artifacts and measured luma (mark 169 vs panel 34, ITU-R 601); observed legible
entries.why: Judgment on the drop: justified as to authority. BRIEF.md line 3 ('Error/retry must be distinguishable without color alone') and line 7 (Paused) bind Retry and Paused, with Ready as a comparison target; the owner's 'readable silhouettes' (line 3) is already bound by readability-1x-3x. Ready alone is not owner-required to pass a grayscale test, so keeping it as a rejection rule would have been a promoted specialist choice. The defect is that the diagnostic was discarded rather than kept advisory; its information supports the later family obligations.
